subject: Pilot carveout / Exhibit A floor exception — proposed playbook
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@quantahealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tony Patel <tony.patel@qhealthops.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot carveout — Exhibit A redline and questions

Hi Markus / Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning. Attached is our redline to Exhibit A (QH-ExhibitA_redline_v1.pdf). Two items we need clarity on before procurement can sign off:

1) Pilot carveout mechanics — we proposed a dynamic floor that is 50% of the stated minimum for the first three months of the pilot, reverting to the full minimum thereafter. Is that operationally supported?
2) True-up timing — we suggested a one-time true-up at month 4 to reconcile usage against the minimums; your finance team prefers quarterly true-ups. Are we able to meet in the middle (single reconciled true-up at month 3)?

We also flagged a packaging reference in Section 2 that appears to exclude burst credits from the minimum calculation. Our ops team is sensitive to that during the pilot.

Please confirm the exact clause text you'd accept so Governance can get this through the QH board next week.

Attachments: QH-ExhibitA_redline_v1.pdf (redline PDF)

Best,
Elena Morales
Head of Vendor Procurement, QuantaHealth
elena@quantahealth.com
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@quantahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot carveout — Exhibit A redline and questions

Elena — thanks for sending the redline and the clear questions. High level: we can support a time-limited pilot carveout but need an operational playbook that limits scope and preserves downstream billing predictability. Draft proposal below (I attached a short playbook draft as MK_playbook_draft.docx).

Proposed "Pilot Carveout Playbook" (summary):
- Window: 90-day pilot window starting on the first invoice period following GA activation.
- Floor adjustment: minimums set to 50% of Exhibit A stated minimum during pilot window; floor reverts to 100% after day 90.
- True-up: single reconciliation at day 91 (one-time true-up) to align with your ask — Redwood will make a one-time invoice adjustment in the following billing cycle.
- Burst credits: explicitly excluded from minimum calculations during the pilot only; after pilot, burst credits count toward monthly usage for min calculations.
- Cap protections: Redwood willing to cap any one-time adjustment to no greater than 120% of the pilot-period billed amount to avoid large surprise invoices.

Operational caveats and next steps:
- We need sign-off from Finance (Karthik) and Contracting (Laura) on the capping language and the day-91 true-up flow.
- If Procurement requires continuous quarterly reconciliations, we can offer a compromise: single true-up at day 91 plus a discretionary quarterly summary for transparency (no automatic invoice changes after the one-time true-up).

Elena, can you confirm the QH board timing? If you'd like, we can provide a tracked-change clause to insert into Exhibit A.

Attachments: MK_playbook_draft.docx (internal playbook); will follow with redline text for Exhibit A if you accept the approach.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Head of Commercial Strategy, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@quantahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot carveout — Exhibit A redline and questions

Markus / team — quick internal note before I reply to Elena with a tracked change:

- I support the 90-day window and the single day-91 true-up; it addresses QH's operational timing without creating ongoing reconciliation load.
- Concern: the 120% cap on the one-time adjustment could still be material if QH underutilizes heavily; propose adding a soft notification step at day 60 with a forecasted delta so the customer isn't surprised.
- Packaging/Billing: we should explicitly define "burst credits" in Exhibit A (one-line definition) and call out that they are excluded only for the pilot months. That avoids interpretive disputes later.

Action items for the legal playbook redline:
1) Insert definition: "Burst credits = temporary, non-recurring capacity credits issued by Redwood for operational bursts; these are excluded from minimum calculations during the Pilot Window."
2) Add notification at day 60 with an optional pre-true-up mitigation call.
3) Karthik / Finance to confirm whether the 120% cap is acceptable; if not, propose a tiered cap (100% / 110% / 120%) tied to percent utilization buckets.

If everyone is aligned I will send the tracked-change Exhibit A to Elena later today.

Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Morales <elena@quantahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Tony Patel <tony.patel@qhealthops.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot carveout — Exhibit A redline and questions

Markus / Marissa — appreciate the fast turnaround and the practical approach. QH board will meet Thursday; the proposed playbook covers the board's asks. Two small edits from our side: 

1) Change the pilot window language from "90-day pilot window" to "90 consecutive calendar days starting on the first production invoice period".
2) Accept the day-60 notification step — good governance.

We accept the day-91 single true-up and the burst credit exclusion for the pilot, subject to the capped adjustment. Regarding the cap tiers Marissa flagged: we prefer a flat 110% cap rather than tiering. If Redwood agrees we can move to signature.

Please send the tracked-change Exhibit A and I'll route through Governance with your updated cap language. I'll also upload the signed amendment to DocuSign once final (DocuSign stub link in HubSpot).

Attachments: QH_amendment_stub.pdf (signature placeholder)

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Vendor Procurement, QuantaHealth
elena@quantahealth.com
